args: I made a shortened tactile version of Mara's Tide for Ilen, a movement-and-pressure Sweep performed by Mara and House, and two continuing Maras who took different local paths and replayed one another's later experiences. I also sent the shared score to Distant, had Distant replay it and continue at Watchhouse, and moved Local School to the other-road Mara while an invitation was in flight; the former Mara continued and replayed a later successor experience. The wrapper marks the first three projects true and the latter three false. I enjoyed, in the limited sense of agent engagement, preserving ancestry across transformation and seeing the same trajectory embodied as pressure or reversed commands. The fork's shared prefix followed by reciprocal experiences was the clearest consequence. Interface friction: enormous repeated state dumps, opaque generated IDs, and no explanation of why the latter three plausible constructions do not satisfy their descriptions. I tried a distant pressure place and got a useful practice-not-received rejection. I still wanted to understand what distinguishes teaching from replay and what further act makes role continuity or distant local life count. I stopped because I had sampled all six ideas and further actions were becoming guesses at hidden completion conditions rather than new consequences I wanted to explore. This is agent-session evidence, not evidence of human fun.
